entries.title: Independent sample coverage
entries.summary: Independent schema-23 evidence narrows sample preservation/module coverage. Other schemas and broader manufacturer/program shapes still lack equivalent independent evidence.

entries.title: Structural validation without authoritative XSD
entries.summary: Imports use bounded structural rules, not authoritative XSD conformance. Unknown constructs are not automatically malformed, understood or editable.

entries.title: Protected project import
entries.summary: ZipCrypto (ETS4/ETS5) decrypts: synthetic fixtures always, the public protected ETS4 and ETS 5.7 samples in an opt-in test since 2026-10-12. AES (ETS6) remains refused; knx diff and product ingest take no password.

entries.title: Imported project default language
entries.summary: Imported projects use an English default, not an inferred authoring language. Product/UI translation choice does not establish project-wide source language.

entries.title: Malformed values and typed mappings
entries.summary: Override fields explicitly retain malformed values. Bare/optional mappings can fall back while reporting the source; retained bytes are not typed interpretation.

entries.title: Native project download streaming
entries.summary: Whole-file response buffering is resolved by streaming. Export still creates a temporary SQLite serialization before responding.

entries.title: CSV interoperability
entries.summary: KNXBench CSV v1 is its own exchange format. Its roundtrip tests do not verify ETS CSV/ESF interoperability.

entries.title: CSV group-range and address operations
entries.summary: CSV does not edit group ranges; removing rows alone does nothing. Explicit moves/deletes reject occupied targets rather than guess swaps.

entries.title: CSV read-only and absent columns
entries.summary: Derived DPT/group columns are read-only; changed values are refused. Description/Comment interchange columns are absent.

entries.title: Spreadsheet transformations
entries.summary: Comma/semicolon separators are supported. Spreadsheet encoding changes or transformed address/boolean cells are not universally accommodated.

entries.title: Project-report parity
entries.summary: HTML documentation is KNXBench's own report. ETS layout/content parity lacks independent reference verification.

entries.title: PDF output
entries.summary: Reports are HTML with print styling and browser print-to-PDF. No native PDF renderer/direct native PDF export is supplied.

entries.title: Report name resolution
entries.summary: Display names require installed matching product data. Unresolved/mismatched references remain raw and reported.

entries.title: Report parameter semantics
entries.summary: Stored values/module arguments are listed with resolvable display names. Raw values are not complete evaluated manufacturer semantics.

entries.title: Report languages
entries.summary: English/German chrome, table labels and product overlays exist (labels since Goal B8). Diagnostic sentences and raw values stay English; no third language.

entries.title: Independent ETS6 object-id evidence
entries.summary: A second independent schema-23 project meets the original lifting condition. Resolution is not arbitrary schema/program coverage or writable module semantics.

entries.title: Project archive budgets and duplicate names
entries.summary: Expanded projects are capped at 1024 MiB total/64 MiB per member. Excess inflation and duplicate/case-colliding names are refused.

entries.title: Overrides outside the active object tree
entries.summary: Unused overrides are retained/reported; conflicting duplicates are errors. No active objects or program defaults are invented.

entries.title: Project user files and add-in payloads
entries.summary: Payloads have bounded descriptive classification but remain opaque data. No unpacking/installation/execution follows.

entries.title: ETS 5.7 schema-20 evidence
entries.summary: Import rests on three public samples. Sub-module object ids and unobserved constructs stay unsupported rather than extrapolated.

entries.title: Import integrity repairs
entries.summary: Repairs do not guess opaque attributes into typed values. Later durable-report delivery supersedes the old persistence gap; channel, address and IP semantics remain bounded.

entries.title: Independent private schema-23 review
entries.summary: One independent project widens import evidence, not universal ETS coverage. Generic findings are documented; original data and raw evidence remain private.

entries.title: Native import evidence and recorded device state
entries.summary: Stored load states are project records, not bus measurements. Missing historical reports are not reconstructed; retained BusAccess/IP configuration is shown read-only since Goal B3, IPConfig without a device.

entries.title: Selective import
entries.summary: Selection merges devices or complete lines into an explicit installation. No building-only selector, automatic readdressing, conflict overwrite or automatic catalogue installation.

entries.title: Parameter evaluation and editing boundaries
entries.summary: Supported top-level and single-authoritative module fields are editable. Calculations, repeated expansion, unsupported controls and encodings remain separately limited. Declared Table/Grid parameter blocks render as a matrix; their visual variants, collapse rules, parameter-driven captions and in-cell buttons are not reproduced.

entries.title: Devices dependent on vendor plug-ins
entries.summary: Vendor-dependent devices remain preservation-only where configuration requires a plug-in. Project app/add-in payloads are retained, not executed by the product.

entries.title: Product schema and namespace coverage
entries.summary: Namespaces have bounded parser/persistence evidence, including exact 10/23 follow-ups. Admission does not establish arbitrary namespaces or all vendor semantics.

entries.title: Manufacturer resolution gaps
entries.summary: Matching product data enriches supported defaults/parameters, not every construct/application combination. Unresolved identities and unsupported semantics stay explicit.

entries.title: Non-program translation semantics
entries.summary: Program/catalogue/hardware/master translations are ingested. Remaining semantics/consumer/language gaps are not blanket loss of Languages blocks.

entries.title: Repeated-module activation
entries.summary: Own instance values are readable without sibling/default substitution. Repeat-driven activation and general repeated-module editing remain unsupported.

entries.title: Modules without identifiers
entries.summary: A Module without Id cannot match stored instance authority. It stays read-only with a diagnostic rather than an invented identity.

entries.title: Writing inactive parameters
entries.summary: Only currently shown/editable panel fields admit writes. Declared but inactive ids are refused.

entries.title: Pre-schema-6 module identities
entries.summary: Migration cannot reconstruct missing original ModuleInstance ids. Re-import is needed to recover authority for scoped editing.

entries.title: Unverified package signatures
entries.summary: Signature members are retained/classified, not verified. Storage does not establish authenticity or trusted origin.

entries.title: Duplicate product identifiers
entries.summary: Normalized duplicates are reported. DPT provenance and unsupported identifier families retain separate boundaries.

entries.title: Re-derivation after parser fixes
entries.summary: Previously derived rows need explicit migration/backfill or fresh ingest. Parser changes do not automatically repair all installed databases.

entries.title: Manufacturer display-name winner
entries.summary: Display names deliberately use last-writer-wins. Ingest order can change names independently of first-winner product definitions.

entries.title: Legacy product import boundaries
entries.summary: VD3–VD5 import is delivered. PR/VD2, legacy DPTs, unsupported parameter forms and unverified hardware downloads remain bounded.

entries.title: Baggage classification versus interpretation
entries.summary: Baggage is inventoried/classified, not installed or executed. Icons/destinations/timestamps remain raw or uninterpreted where documented.

entries.title: Product and application identity policy
entries.summary: Winner/candidate provenance is reported; first-installed definitions still win. No version selector, pinning or compatibility/replacement policy exists.

entries.title: Object activation and DPT gaps
entries.summary: Labels/bounded evaluation exist. Undetermined activation, unsupported scoped sets and missing DPTs are explicit, not inferred.

entries.title: Resolved product filename case handling
entries.summary: ASCII-case-independent extensions resolve the uppercase refusal. Namespace/archive/legacy limits remain.

entries.title: Resolved nested-module storage
entries.summary: The database-constraint defect is fixed. Successful install does not prove nested Dynamic/editing/download semantics.

entries.title: Product-package size profiles
entries.summary: Explicit bounded profiles admit larger measured bundles; production/web limits remain. Corpus inclusion is not unlimited admission/hardware verification.

entries.title: XML evidence budgets
entries.summary: Measured refusals have a bounded delivered remedy, not unlimited XML processing. Coupled byte/item/depth limits and atomic refusal remain.

entries.title: Exact product namespaces 10 and 23
entries.summary: Exact 10/23 parsing/persistence is admitted. Historical refusals do not describe current unknown-vendor/other-namespace support.

entries.title: Parameter-attribute reporting
entries.summary: Previously unreported attributes are now retained/reported at scoped ingestion. Reporting grants no typed semantics/editing/image materialization.

entries.title: AP3 bounded parameter controls
entries.summary: Time retains counts; sliders need bounded integer evidence. Colour/Picture stay unsupported-codec originals; modules need separate mapping contracts.

entries.title: Catalogue batch creation
entries.summary: Creation is bounded to 1–32 devices and one undo step. Unique names/address allocation are explicit options, not default deduplication or physical commissioning.

entries.title: Catalogue metadata semantics
entries.summary: Secure/version/capacity attributes remain manufacturer source strings, not parsed capabilities or compatibility policy.

entries.title: Catalogue updates from supplied files
entries.summary: Updates use user-supplied files, not the KNX Online Catalog. Full database backups and plain install are separate from the reviewed update/restore workflow.

entries.title: Checked parameter editors
entries.summary: Checked controls are opt-in and bounded; modules fall back, Colour/Picture remain unconverted originals. Writes are revision-bound end to end since Goal B1a.

entries.title: Manufacturer report history
entries.summary: Measured facts require encounter-ledger evidence; older installs are unavailable, not zero. Reports do not interpret all vendor semantics or verify signatures.

entries.title: Parameter and Dynamic coverage
entries.summary: Unsupported layouts, calculations, activation and encodings remain named limits. Grid declarations can render as lists; retained values do not prove editable semantics.

entries.title: Binary project files and version control
entries.summary: SQLite projects do not yield meaningful textual VCS diffs. Application comparison exists; no independent textual project interchange format is supplied.

entries.title: Resolved imported-project store path
entries.summary: Project replacement clears the prior native save target. The old stale-path overwrite scenario is resolved and retained historically.

entries.title: Resolved save-helper claims
entries.summary: The compatibility helper uses transactional whole-project saving, not a live row-incremental engine. Earlier no-op/persistence overclaims are resolved.

entries.title: Project-comparison parity
entries.summary: KNXBench defines independent comparison rules. Equivalent ETS matching/content behavior is unverified.

entries.title: Device matching without stable keys
entries.summary: Devices lacking address/matching ETS id cannot be confidently correlated. Serial/Puid stability is not guessed into a replacement key.

entries.title: Duplicate building-part names in comparison
entries.summary: Same-named sibling paths produce ambiguity and adds/removes. The comparer does not arbitrarily match them.

entries.title: Regenerated ETS identifiers
entries.summary: Regenerated identifiers can appear as adds/removes when natural keys differ. No special re-import identity inference is supplied.

entries.title: Applying or merging project diffs
entries.summary: Comparison is read-only, with no atomic diff-to-command merge engine. Conflict/identity/unsupported-field semantics remain prerequisites.

entries.title: Three-way comparison
entries.summary: Only two projects are compared. No common-ancestor-aware comparison or merge workflow exists.

entries.title: Site and building evidence
entries.summary: Ground roots group buildings on one installation based on schema/synthetic evidence. Independent ETS examples and multi-installation Sites remain separate gaps.

entries.title: Allocator safeguards and deferred enforcement
entries.summary: Collision/rewind/exhaustion data-loss paths are closed. Structural enforcement phases 3–5 remain explicitly deferred.

entries.title: In-place native project migration
entries.summary: The first write into an older project upgrades the original in place; opening and every reading command use an in-memory copy. Atomic migration is not backup; older builds refuse newer schemas.

entries.title: New-project wizard presets
entries.summary: The wizard seeds one installation from bounded fixed presets. It does not model every vocabulary or multi-installation design.

entries.title: Add-device preview freshness
entries.summary: Preview confirms names/addresses, not immutable project/catalogue state. Other concurrent changes can still refuse creation.

entries.title: Raw rich-text header candidates
entries.summary: Candidates are exposed without rendering/format certification. Bounded instruction editing is separate; no general rich-text catalogue/RTF decoder is claimed.

entries.title: Device editor address scope
entries.summary: Device-octet editing is line-bound; new .0 addresses require coupler evidence. Project edits do not program physical addresses or infer missing product identity.

entries.title: Group-address membership and download preparation
entries.summary: Linking follows actual installation ownership. Selection/preparation guide existing routes, not new write permission or hardware verification.

entries.title: Historical native notes foundation
entries.summary: Local-only/no-editor wording is superseded by service/workbench delivery. Literal text, selective note import and downgrade limits remain.

entries.title: Installation instruction editing
entries.summary: Editing admits bounded exact-source Schema23 XML and selected text/header forms, and devices made in KNXBench (no invented original, Goal B4). Other schemas, encodings, ambiguous owners and unsupported formats remain explicit refusals.

entries.title: Instruction and note drafts across Save
entries.summary: Drafts survive Save when server content is unchanged. Real changes require comparison/discard; reloads ask through the engine's own prompt in the browser and, since Goal B2, the desktop webview (not run natively).

entries.title: Notes editor integration
entries.summary: The notes leaf is now hosted; its unmounted status is historical. Unknown transport outcomes require reload, and working history is not implicit Save.

entries.title: Offline naming recipes
entries.summary: Recipes rename explicitly ordered existing addresses only. Conflicts require re-preview; durable working history is not root Save, templates or bus operation.

entries.title: Persistent native working history
entries.summary: Edits may be journaled before Save; closing without Save does not erase the journal. Same-database versions are not independent backups or multi-user history.

entries.title: Project-local name editing
entries.summary: Individual names are guarded edits, not bulk templates or inferred names. Imported exceptions stay preserved; offline projections cannot authorize writes.

entries.title: Project notes workbench
entries.summary: Notes use real project targets; ambiguous identities are withheld. Browser prompts, desktop reloads and translated review text retain disclosed platform/language boundaries.

entries.title: Structure editor scope
entries.summary: Commands respect installation ownership and refuse ambiguous/cross-installation moves. This is not general multi-installation transfer or topology-compatibility validation.

entries.title: Bounded commissioning support
entries.summary: Memory downloads have scoped evidence, not general device support. Public K6/serial/K13 address writes fail before a tunnel without specific durable recovery. Project/device comparison is a session observation; unknown fields remain explicit beside raw ranges, and relevant edits invalidate tags.

entries.title: Simulator versus hardware evidence
entries.summary: Simulator coverage exceeds recorded device runs. Limited live experiments do not validate every mask/recovery case/vendor program.

entries.title: Declarative procedure version writes
entries.summary: The illustrative core model still lists unconditional version writes. It is not the narrower executed sequencer or a universal write script.

entries.title: Documented specification contradictions
entries.summary: Explicit rulings handle named standard contradictions. They grant no permission to infer unrelated undocumented behavior.

entries.title: Memory-control access-nibble inference
entries.summary: Nibble order is inferred from table position, not explicit text. This inference is not independent wire-level evidence.

entries.title: Load-state retry latency
entries.summary: The prescribed extra poll can include sleep, reconnect and retries. Waiting can exceed a simple transition-time estimate.

entries.title: Reconnect cost during quiet completion
entries.summary: Released connections can require a full reconnect for each quiet LoadCompleting poll. Tolerated silence can still be costly.

entries.title: Control-frame on-wire priority
entries.summary: Constructed frames request SYSTEM priority. No independent TP1 trace proves gateway preservation of that priority.

entries.title: Occupied-address specification ruling
entries.summary: The procedure follows MP's exception interpretation where wording conflicts. Public address-write recovery restrictions remain.

entries.title: Repeated download part kinds
entries.summary: Two parts of the same PartKind are refused because order is undefined. Arbitrary segment ordering is not invented.

entries.title: PL110 group-responser table
entries.summary: PID_GROUP_RESPONSER_TABLE is unimplemented. PL110-specific obligations do not imply medium support or applicability elsewhere.

entries.title: Individual-address unload
entries.summary: Destructive address unload is unimplemented. Removing a management address requires separately verified recovery.

entries.title: Access-key assignment during download
entries.summary: Required A_Key_Write plans are refused. Using an existing key does not support assigning/changing keys.

entries.title: Partial-download escalation scope
entries.summary: Escalation reloads only carried segments. It does not reconstruct omitted parts or imply a complete-device reload.

entries.title: Download-counter refusal policy
entries.summary: Changed/unavailable counters trigger conservative refusal. This is KNXBench policy, not a universal System B obligation.

entries.title: Recovery and restart waits
entries.summary: Typed callers honor scoped waits. No generic failed-service retry policy or universal hardware recovery follows.

entries.title: Individual-address write procedure
entries.summary: The procedure does not loop indefinitely for programming mode and uses a disclosed release interpretation. Public writes remain recovery-gated.

entries.title: 0701h download and restart evidence
entries.summary: Evidence covers identified programs/devices. The named MDT's Basic Restart stays unacknowledged, not a verified restart.

entries.title: Download authorization key provenance
entries.summary: Keys come from project attributes or explicit input. Simulator/routes do not prove live validation of a device key.

entries.title: Serial-number address-write evidence
entries.summary: The device ignored the tested write; sending is not confirmation. Public serial writes stay recovery-gated.

entries.title: Individual-address reset boundary
entries.summary: HTTP/UI reset is excluded by decision. Historical restart uncertainty remains; public writes fail closed without recovery.

entries.title: Master Reset evidence
entries.summary: Simulator erase coverage exists; recorded hardware kept its configuration. Successful physical erase/universal recovery is unproved.

entries.title: Partial-download evidence
entries.summary: UI/backend scopes are delivered with single-device evidence. Other products/images, escalation and recovery remain separately bounded.

entries.title: RF domain-address scope
entries.summary: Domain-address procedures are simulator-tested only. Hardware writes are refused; broader RF/PL110 support is not implied.

entries.title: RF configuration scope
entries.summary: Configuration is simulator-only, with no supported hardware write/CLI/HTTP admission. No KNX-RF validation is claimed.

entries.title: Unlinked active communication objects
entries.summary: Instance overrides reach active tables, but unlinked objects can differ from ETS images. Read-back comparison is not a download witness.

entries.title: Parameter byte-order download boundary
entries.summary: Unverified LittleEndian materialization remains refused. Defaults/base-image probes and tester reports define no per-type encoding or new write permission.

entries.title: UTF-8 text download encoding
entries.summary: Encoding is refused without a sufficient manufacturer/payload contract. Research does not justify guessed bytes or hardware changes.

entries.title: Stored loaded-image semantics
entries.summary: LoadedImage/CheckSums are retained, not decoded/verified as reusable download images. Preservation does not establish encoding/compatibility.

entries.title: Accepted commissioning validation boundary
entries.summary: New hardware, power-loss, vendor and ETS experiments were removed by user decision. This grants neither new write permission nor compatibility/recovery guarantees.

entries.title: Backup directory synchronization
entries.summary: Synced directory chains are not disk-loss or confinement proof. Paths must stay stable; failed diagnostic files are not recovery receipts.

entries.title: Download lifecycle history
entries.summary: Admission/lifecycle records are bounded, not full audit/traffic/recovery history. Durable metadata does not prove whole-device recovery.

entries.title: Download readiness and pre-write backup
entries.summary: A plannable default image is not hardware verification. Readiness is application/download-type scoped; backups cover only declared pre-write recovery boundaries.

entries.title: Offline AP1 sequence inspection
entries.summary: Only explicit, uniquely associated MV-07B0 Load/ap1 declarations are reconstructed. Unsupported steps stay reported; inspection adds no download/execution capability.

entries.title: KNXnet/IP protocol scope
entries.summary: Tunnelling/routing/discovery have bounded implementations. Ordinary connectivity does not imply KNX IP Secure or extended discovery support.

entries.title: CLI monitor formatting
entries.summary: Lifted by AR14: monitor and write use the --project style and show every installation's name. Three-level remains without --project and for route-send; joined names are not escaped.

entries.title: Custom routing multicast evidence
entries.summary: Custom routing multicast selection is validated. Discovery/real custom-group traffic do not inherit verification from default paths or offline tests.

entries.title: Session-log export window
entries.summary: Only retained capped entries/loss counts are exported. Evicted entries, replaced-project history and prior runs cannot be reconstructed; raw logs may identify projects.

entries.title: DPT codec coverage
entries.summary: Main types 1–30 have explicit formats/rulings; subtype/FB semantics remain partial. Unsupported structured types and generic parameter-only writes are not silently admitted.

entries.title: Group Monitor evidence
entries.summary: The GUI is tunnelling-based, single-session and client-filtered. Passive receive evidence does not verify every send/device/routing/history scenario.

entries.title: Line-scan duration and bus load
entries.summary: Sequential probing takes significant time and holds a tunnel. Pacing/exclusions mitigate cost; there is no instantaneous whole-line scan.

entries.title: Line-scan identity limits
entries.summary: Scans establish occupancy/mask version, not product, manufacturer or serial identity. Those facts are not inferred.

entries.title: Busy devices and vacant scan results
entries.summary: Negative/missing confirms can yield the same vacant verdict. Busy devices are not reliably distinguished from absent addresses.

entries.title: Short scan timeouts
entries.summary: Shorter timeouts trade evidence for speed and can mark slow devices vacant. Silence is not proof of absence.

entries.title: Scan shortcuts and ambiguous probes
entries.summary: Negative confirms have no fast vacancy path; dropped-frame ambiguity is not automatically retried. These are explicit scan policies.

entries.title: Single-line scan scope
entries.summary: One line is scanned sequentially through one gateway. No automatic coupler traversal or multi-line scan.

entries.title: Gateway endpoints in scan results
entries.summary: Only the scan's own tunnel address is excluded. Other endpoints can appear occupied without identifying physical devices.

entries.title: Discovery reachability
entries.summary: Discovery needs multicast and permitted unicast replies. Manual endpoints/host networking do not eliminate firewall, routing, capacity or bridge-HPAI constraints.

entries.title: Monitor-context freshness
entries.summary: Server-authoritative polling supersedes the browser-only stale lock. It is not cross-server coordination or complete traffic/audit history.

entries.title: Historical DPT count correction
entries.summary: 46 was a catalogue count, not main type 46. This planning correction creates no codec support or new task.

entries.title: Write-echo error branch
entries.summary: A typed decode-error branch exists without a known honest end-to-end public-API trigger. Type coverage is not a real-trigger witness.

entries.title: Discovery metadata display
entries.summary: Decoded optional metadata is shown; missing fields stay unavailable. Loopback/browser evidence is not real multicast/hardware verification.

entries.title: Scan reconciliation is occupancy-based
entries.summary: Unexpected responses create product-less devices. Silence is not absence; deletions require explicit selection.

entries.title: Monitor capture retention
entries.summary: Captures are retained windows with separate server-loss/client-pruning counts. Pause cannot recover traffic; exports are size-bounded.

entries.title: Telegram-flow evidence and capacity
entries.summary: Chromium readability/layout evidence has bounded capacity. Membership/inference is not measured delivery/device state; native/accessibility remains separate.

entries.title: Named gateway refusals
entries.summary: Holder details cover this server's sessions only. Other clients are known through gateway refusal; timeout is not proof of busy.

entries.title: Bus-activity snapshot
entries.summary: The partial server-lifetime snapshot is not a complete audit or device-mutation proof. Polling can miss actions; empty sessions do not prove gateway idleness.

entries.title: Name-first DPT presentation
entries.summary: Names are a display vocabulary, not codec/device support. Unknown/main-only identifiers stay exact; stored data, diagnostics and exports are not rewritten.

entries.title: Telegram-flow delivery and scope
entries.summary: Flow is implemented; approval-only wording is historical. Configured participants are not measured recipients/device state; Chromium/capacity limits remain in KL-154.

entries.title: Overlay accessibility evidence
entries.summary: Shared modal/keyboard behavior is implemented. Scoped fixes do not certify complete accessibility, screen-reader or native WebKitGTK conformance.

entries.title: File picker upload and selection
entries.summary: Multi-file upload/drop is implemented; project selection remains singular. Cancellation is not rollback of an upload already sent.

entries.title: Translation coverage
entries.summary: Overlays reach selected surfaces, not every imported text or UI output. Fallback labels and untranslated technical detail remain visible.

entries.title: Motion controls and residual surfaces
entries.summary: Global/per-category controls exist. Recorded surface, lifecycle and native/accessibility limits remain; controls are not an every-effect guarantee.

entries.title: Project-diff table presentation
entries.summary: Filtered virtualized entity tables are implemented. Display adds no apply/merge capability or universal matching guarantee.

entries.title: Technical prose localization
entries.summary: Translated diagnostics expose raw English detail on request. This is not complete localization or reconstruction of every controlling source fact.

entries.title: Indeterminate import progress
entries.summary: Most phases expose truthful labels, not percentages. Smooth completion requires totals the implementation does not know.

entries.title: Load-banner message timing
entries.summary: Short loads show few rotating messages. Rotation targets long loads and never deliberately delays work.

entries.title: Help text format
entries.summary: Help consists of plain translation-key paragraphs. No Markdown/rich-text help engine or per-topic help store exists.

entries.title: Cross-window preference refresh
entries.summary: Visible windows refresh periodically/on focus. Bounded synchronization is not user isolation or native-platform verification.

entries.title: Application zoom
entries.summary: Zoom is bounded to 80–150% in 10% steps. Browser evidence does not prove native focus/resize/accessibility parity.

entries.title: Shared first-run guide state
entries.summary: Guide state is per installation, not person. Fresh concurrent windows can both show it; dismissal affects all server users.

entries.title: Shared achievement counters
entries.summary: Counters are installation-wide and UI-only. Since 13 October 2026 concurrent steps add up (deduplicated over the last 1,024 batches). Hidden catalogue entries are not secrets.

entries.title: Group-address picker matching
entries.summary: Search is substring-per-word with caller order, not fuzzy ranking. DPT marks disclose identities, not device compatibility.

entries.title: Tree indentation limits
entries.summary: Indentation caps at depth 12; flat views stay flat. Measured channel fixes do not establish every grouped-table layout.

entries.title: Communication-object table
entries.summary: DPT labels and object presentation do not establish manufacturer semantics. Raw references, effective flags and missing metadata retain separate provenance.

entries.title: CRT motion
entries.summary: Motion is a separate preference, not executable theme-pack behavior. Save glow marks activation, not success; Chromium fixtures do not prove native persistence/accessibility.

entries.title: Current-project device navigation
entries.summary: Links resolve unique current-project devices, not physical/historical hardware. Metadata, large-project rendering and native/accessibility evidence remain bounded.

entries.title: Four group-address views
entries.summary: The matrix includes linked objects plus explicitly loaded device objects, not an automatic whole-project inventory. Views add no hardware model/direct matrix writes.

entries.title: Import-count links and unsaved-change dialogs
entries.summary: Import links show a capped current-run log, which may hold fewer findings than the report. Shared Chromium-tested dialogs do not establish native behavior.

entries.title: Installation-node editing
entries.summary: Unnamed nodes are readable and renameable; the rename route accepts a revision binding the web editor does not send yet. This is not a general installation-management workflow.

entries.title: LCARS presentation
entries.summary: Built-in framing is not executable imported geometry or lossless v1 export. Native WebKitGTK, Orca and complete WCAG/browser acceptance remain unverified.

entries.title: Ported UX feedback limits
entries.summary: Toast queues, flow-image exports and motion controls are bounded presentation. Waiting cards can drop; snapshots/notifications do not establish device success or full history.

entries.title: Theme pack management
entries.summary: Declarative pack management is delivered, not universal extension compatibility. Native/accessibility and broader format capabilities retain their recorded boundaries.

entries.title: KNX Secure runtime
entries.summary: Research adds no Secure runtime, keyring decoding, AES-project import or credential vault. Retained/native backups may contain sensitive material.

entries.title: GTK3 desktop dependency
entries.summary: The desktop remains GTK3-based. Withdrawn maintenance advisories provide neither a GTK4 port nor broader native-platform validation.

entries.title: Server authentication and exposure
entries.summary: One password is not per-user rights or internet-security certification. Host-network exposure requires trusted LAN/VPN/firewall; unauthenticated listeners remain host-loopback-only.

entries.title: Shared server project and undo stack
entries.summary: Clients share one project/undo stack. Feature-specific guards are not general concurrent-edit isolation, accounts or collaboration.

entries.title: Version identity and dirty builds
entries.summary: Version output identifies the build commit, not uncommitted state. No dirty-tree marker guarantees exact build provenance.

entries.title: Debug-report privacy limits
entries.summary: Redaction covers named patterns only. Source/XML/endpoints can identify projects; reports/native exports are not comprehensive anonymization.

entries.title: Resolved gate-root validation
entries.summary: Runtime workspace-root validation resolves this gate defect. Historical evidence does not certify every unrelated tool's root handling.

entries.title: Terminated versus hung webviews
entries.summary: Terminated processes can reload; hangs without termination remain a native close/recovery limitation. Chromium cannot settle that case.

entries.title: Bridge-network tunnel reachability
entries.summary: Route-Back has offline evidence; real bridged tunnels remain unverified. Linux host networking is the workaround, not elimination of multicast/gateway constraints.

entries.title: AppImage display-backend evidence
entries.summary: Source no longer universally forces X11. Old assets and one-host native startup evidence do not establish every-host compatibility.

entries.title: Older desktop data-folder transition
entries.summary: Alpha.5 changed the identifier without automatic alpha.4 data migration. Copy preserved data deliberately; an empty new library is not evidence of deletion.

entries.title: Server shutdown and active writes
entries.summary: A stop refuses new bus jobs and waits a bounded, configurable time for a running download/address programming; a write still running when that ends, or under SIGKILL, is cut mid-way.

entries.title: Docker release-image publication
entries.summary: Images follow tags; latest may be an alpha. Provenance is not signing; base updates do not follow every source commit.

entries.title: Browser upload and navigation limits
entries.summary: Raw/member/XML budgets remain; large admission proves neither full scanning nor bounded memory. Return navigation reloads the editor.

entries.title: AppImage Mesa EGL compatibility
entries.summary: The alpha.9-and-earlier libwayland failure has a scoped launcher fix. One-host repair does not guarantee every Mesa/EGL/display backend.

entries.title: Desktop export commands
entries.summary: AppImages up to alpha.11 refuse saving the session log and monitor captures; fixed in source, ships with the next AppImage. Web and Docker unaffected.

entries.title: Desktop silent downloads
entries.summary: AppImages up to alpha.11 save in-app downloads silently into Downloads, replacing same-named files; fixed in source with a save dialog. Web and Docker unaffected.

entries.title: Project files without their manufacturer files
entries.summary: A .knxdb saved before store schema v16 does not carry its application programs; next to an empty product database its devices show no parameters until restored from the original .knxproj. Fixed for new saves.

entries.title: Extension API scope
entries.summary: No general third-party format/protocol/UI plug-in API exists. Declarative configuration is not executable runtime extension support.

entries.title: MCP state and visibility boundaries
entries.summary: Read tools expose bounded project evidence; visibility is not access authorization. Opt-in literal renames are separate, not general project mutation.

entries.title: Community support evidence
entries.summary: Sharing is manual and potentially identifying; raw originals are not anonymized. Scanning/redaction is bounded; cancellation does not synchronously stop server parsing.

entries.title: Fictional community demos
entries.summary: Demos are offline learning data with fictional products, not electrical designs or verified ETS/device programs. Never download their programs to hardware.

entries.title: MCP rename confirmation
entries.summary: The opt-in writer permits literal group-address renames through client form elicitation. It cannot prove a human answered or establish operator identity.

entries.title: Release notifications
entries.summary: GitHub polling is not instant notification, installation or integrity verification. Offline/rate-limited responses cannot establish the newest release; opt-out cannot recall sent requests.

entries.title: Website and public story
entries.summary: Chromium/publication/video evidence does not certify all browsers, accessibility, performance or hardware. Privacy/legal text has no legal-compliance certification.

entries.title: Rewritten Git commit identities
entries.summary: Pre-7-October citations may reference rewritten hashes. Use the historical map rather than assume evidence is absent.

entries.title: Alpha.8 release snapshot
entries.summary: This dated release record is historical. Preserved-source evidence does not imply complete ETS semantics, export/signing or wider hardware eligibility.

entries.title: Closed entries and legacy links
entries.summary: Removed/withdrawn entries retain historical anchors and evidence links. Numbers stay reserved and are not reopened by reorganization.

entries.title: Historical reading guide
entries.summary: The 8 October audit is a dated interpretation guide, not the current feature inventory or a new work assignment.

entries.title: Diagnostic export reads identity only
entries.summary: The read-only diagnostic export reads descriptor, PID12 and PID78 only; no memory profile is admitted, a zero-element reply cannot separate refusal from absence, and no physical device has been read with it yet.

entries.title: Git history rewritten; GitHub pull-request refs keep old commits
entries.summary: History, messages and tags were rewritten on 2026-10-17 (map COMMIT_MAP_2026-10-17); GitHub still serves the pre-rewrite commits through two read-only pull-request refs and the fork.

entries.title: Plug-in data adoption is not undoable; adopted bytes are unverified
entries.summary: Adopting a plug-in's stored bytes between two projects of one lineage exists in the application layer, the CLI and (since 17 October 2026) the server and web app. The bytes are not decoded, no remapping is attempted, the opaque store is outside command Undo (the way back is a project version recorded before the change), and no plug-in, ETS or device acceptance of the adopted bytes is verified.
